solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lark in flight embracing the beginning of another day

indicators.note: embracing means the word for flight wraps around the letter that follows

parts.note: an escape is a flight from captivity

indicators.note: the beginning of picks out only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A skylark soaring away and taking in the start of another day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lark' looks like the bird the surface flies, but it is the definition in its sense of a prank; A and D go inside ESCAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of mischievous fun, a prank or adventurous caper.

clue.text: Make a strenuous effort to overwhelm Penny with an ace

indicators.note: to overwhelm means the effort word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to exert oneself is to make a strenuous effort

explanation.surface: Trying hard to crush the coins with a top card.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is someone highly skilled, a master of their field.

clue.text: Fled northward taken in by scoundrel's false report

indicators.note: taken in by means the reversed letters sit inside the scoundrel

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel

indicators.note: northward in a down clue means the letters read upward, so backwards

parts.note: ran means fled

explanation.surface: A villain who ran off north spreads a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northward' works because in a down clue, letters read upward come out backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is an unfounded rumour or story, a hoax.

clue.text: Beat poet's opening line dividing American enthusiasts at first

indicators.note: opening picks out the first letter of the poet
dividing means the line letter splits the American letters
at first takes only the opening letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A Beat poet starts a verse that splits American fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat poet' suggests Kerouac or Ginsberg; Beat is the definition, a throb.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the regular throb of the heart, a beat.

clue.text: Leaves from unfamiliar trees in the centre of Pudsey

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the centre letters
the centre of takes the middle letters of the town name
unfamiliar says the letters of trees are set in a strange order

explanation.surface: Foliage from exotic trees in the middle of a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Pudsey is a town near Leeds; its middle letters DS hold ESERT, the anagram of TREES. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert someone is to leave them, abandoning them.

clue.text: Well-known for earliest of five love affairs after binning Rex

indicators.note: earliest of takes just the first letter of the next word
after binning says a letter is thrown out of the word before it

parts.note: amours are love affairs
Rex, Latin for king, is abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A celebrity is notorious for a handful of romances once the king is out of the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rex' (king) gives R, which is removed from AMOURS to leave AMOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being widely known is exactly what it means to have fame; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pick up twig

definitions.meaning: to pick someone up is to arrest them
to twig is to catch on or understand

explanation.walkthrough: 'twig' looks like a small branch but is the verb meaning grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprehend is both to arrest a suspect and to grasp an idea.

clue.text: Yielding to revolutionary over plot that's Chinese essentially

indicators.note: over means the turned word covers the following letters around them
revolutionary says the little word is turned round

parts.note: taken as written
a bed is a plot in a garden
that's means that is, abbreviated i.e.

indicators.note: essentially picks the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Submitting to a rebel after a plot that is basically Chinese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is used as a container: the turned word sits over and around the rest. The centre letter of the seven-letter word Chinese is its fourth.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliant and willing to follow orders, giving way to authority.

clue.text: Go on the radio in support of amiable climber

indicators.note: in support of in a down clue means it sits below the next part

parts.note: sweet means amiable or kind

indicators.note: on the radio says the word is heard spoken, not seen

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to pee

explanation.surface: A friendly broadcaster takes to the airwaves to back a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' sounds like a mountaineer but is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing plant grown for its scented flowers.

clue.text: Incurable optimist's long pass goes wrong

indicators.note: goes wrong says the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A football fan stays hopeful even as a long ball goes astray.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Pangloss is the relentlessly optimistic tutor in Voltaire's Candide; 's here stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Pangloss in Voltaire's Candide insists all is for the best, so his name stands for a hopeless optimist.

clue.text: A financial share for each person

parts.note: a piece, as in a piece of the action, is a share of money

explanation.surface: One stake in a business divided equally per head.
explanation.definitionFit: Each one is counted separately, so a share given per head is given to every individual in turn.

clue.text: Almost shot getting caught with it

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for shot is dropped

parts.note: a chip is a short lofted shot in golf
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Almost getting the shot when a ball is caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fashionable and up to date, stylish.

clue.text: Unusual world of American rock band

parts.note: rare means unusual
the earth is our world

explanation.surface: A strange planet belonging to a US group of rockers.
explanation.walkthrough: Rare Earth were a Motown rock band of the late 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare Earth was an American rock group signed to Motown, known for Get Ready.

clue.text: Be without at first

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of or without, as in ex dividend
first is written 1st, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: To go without at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link; 1ST becomes IST when the figure one is read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is simply to have being, to live or be present in the world.

clue.text: Heads for university on New Street going west

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the university letter comes straight after the new letter
going west in an across clue means the street letters are read right to left

explanation.surface: Directions for students heading west along a new street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for heads, as in using your nut.

clue.text: Intrigue against union leader and end with miners mostly in revolt

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of the word union
in revolt says the letters rise up and scatter
mostly drops the final letter of the miners

explanation.surface: A strike leader plots to finish off the pits with the coal workers in rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts MINERS to MINER; END plus MINER is rearranged as NDERMINE. 'and', 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To undermine is to weaken someone secretly, to plot against them.

clue.text: Can see about grasping a bit of life being free from guilt

indicators.note: grasping means the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
about here signals the letters of the two words are scattered and reset
a bit of takes only the first letter of the word after

explanation.surface: Someone sees a bit of life as a way of being cleared of sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' shuffles CAN SEE into CEANSE, and 'grasping' puts L from 'life' inside, giving CLEANSE. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To purify someone morally is to wash away their sin, making them clean in conscience.

clue.text: Appropriate getting a constituent to join in

parts.note: to appropriate is to take
a part is a constituent of a whole

explanation.surface: Fitting getting a voter to participate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituent' suggests a voter, but it is a component.
explanation.definitionFit: To participate is to join in an activity.

clue.text: Ended having spoken of rural life

parts.note: past means finished or over
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: Finished having talked about country living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral writing or painting idealises the life of the countryside.

clue.text: Relinquish part of contraband only

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Give up just a portion of the smuggled goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or let go of something entirely, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Wicked town? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Neath is a town in South Wales

explanation.surface: Is this a wicked town? Not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' here is slang for excellent, as is neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang terms of approval meaning great or excellent.

clue.text: Roughly made cross by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for cross is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, especially in a church

explanation.surface: Something crudely built that seems irritated when heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry', but here it is a crucifix, a rood.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude or primitive in construction, as in a basic hut put together roughly.

clue.text: Dad finding German mare let loose outside in storm

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled letters surround dad
let loose says the horse and letter are scrambled

parts.note: pa is a word for dad

explanation.surface: Dad finds the German horse running wild in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let loose' turns G plus MARE into RAMGE, which goes outside PA. 'finding' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to storm about violently and wildly.

clue.text: Snippet of goss? Tenor has it repeated about bass

indicators.note: about means the repeated words go around the next letter
repeated means the small word is written twice

explanation.surface: A tenor has a bit of gossip repeated about a bass singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a tasty morsel, here of news or gossip.

clue.text: Strengthen old queen before return of the French

parts.note: Queen Anne reigned from 1702 to 1714

indicators.note: return of says the French article is read backwards

parts.note: la is French for the

explanation.surface: Toughen an old monarch before the return of the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is a link that puts the queen first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal glass or metal is to heat and cool it slowly to toughen it.

clue.text: Come in time to block French fellow from the rear

indicators.note: to block means the time letter sits inside the reversed name
from the rear says the name is read starting at its end

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: Arriving at a moment that stops a Frenchman from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the rear' turns RENE into ENER; T goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into a room or place is to come in; a plain synonym.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of truth from Democrat hiding in American embassy

indicators.note: hiding in means the Democrat letter is tucked inside the following words

parts.note: a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: A political party member confesses while sheltering in a US diplomatic post.
explanation.definitionFit: A confession owning up to a fact is an acknowledgement that something is true.

clue.text: Evident in Assad humbled by a holy man

indicators.note: evident in says the answer can be seen within the following words

explanation.surface: A Syrian leader brought low by a holy man is evident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu ascetic or holy man.

clue.text: Resourceful soldiers back lining mine opening

indicators.note: lining means the reversed letters sit inside the mine entrance

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine

indicators.note: back says the soldiers' letters are read in reverse

parts.note: OR, other ranks, stands for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Clever troops return to reinforce the entrance of a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is a crossword staple for soldiers; an adit is a level tunnel into a hillside mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skilful and quick-witted in handling situations, a close synonym of clever and resourceful.

clue.text: Noble reportedly talented is deserving of praise

indicators.note: reportedly says these words are heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a noble is a lord, a peer of the realm
able means talented or capable

explanation.surface: A gifted aristocrat is said to merit applause.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound alike in a non-rhotic British accent, which drops the R. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthy of being lauded, or praised, is commendable.

clue.text: Cashier to spill the beans about retiring

parts.note: to tell is to reveal a secret

indicators.note: retiring says the word for about is drawn backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A bank clerk is reluctant to blab about a shy colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank employee who counts money in and out at the counter is a bank cashier.

clue.text: Refutation by contrary argument not assumed to implicate Bottom

indicators.note: to implicate means to fold the next item inside

parts.note: something real is genuine, not assumed or pretended
butt is slang for the bottom

explanation.surface: A counter-argument that drags in Bottom, the weaver from A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' looks like Shakespeare's weaver, but it is a backside, a BUTT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal answers a claim with evidence or argument against it.
